title: PFASware: Quantifying the Environmental Impact of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) in Computing Systems
problem: Computing systems manufacturing uses PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl forever chemicals) extensively. Need to quantify environmental impact and identify design optimizations to reduce PFAS use.
motivation: PFAS bioaccumulative and persistent; IC manufacturing accounts for 10% of PFAS-containing fluoropolymers in Europe. Regulatory scrutiny increasing; design-phase optimization opportunities.
method: Quantify PFAS volume in IC designs across process nodes (7nm, 16nm, 28nm) and lithography methods (EUV vs DUV immersion). Compare PFAS footprint across design choices.
key_novelty: Quantifying PFAS environmental footprint in IC design and demonstrating optimization via lithography/node selection.
contributions: Quantified PFAS volume for IC designs at multiple technology nodes
20% PFAS reduction achievable with EUV vs DUV at 7nm

metrics.other: PFAS volume reduction 20% (EUV vs DUV), 15% (16nm vs 28nm)

limitations: Analysis limited to IC manufacturing; impact of other electronics (displays, batteries) mentioned but not quantified.
